display.title: Episode 339: The Storyteller, Chapter 2 (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul)
display.summary_short: A listener's poems from the mailbox, the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class says Shema, the Baal Shem Tov's shamash sets out as a storyteller, and a lesson on Modeh Ani.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Elul 5748. Uncle Yossi dives into his overflowing mailbox and reads a young listener's three poems about Torah, Avodah and tzedakah, the three things the world stands on. After the Hakochainik march, story time begins 'The Storyteller': at the Baal Shem Tov's bedside, his faithful shamash Rabbi Yehuda is told to travel and tell stories, and promised that this will make him rich. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school then recites the Shema in Studio 604. Back in the story, Rabbi Yehuda sets out, and his first listener, a hotel owner, pays him only three kopecks; disappointed but trusting, he resolves not to give up. Uncle Yossi announces Shabbos Mevarchim for Elul, the last month of the year, and teaches hakaras hatov through Modeh Ani, the first thank-you of the day, with a song to sing it to. The show closes with candle-lighting time and the Dial-a-Jewish-Story line.
display.lesson: Never give up and trust in Hashem; and start every day, and every kindness you receive, with a thank-you.
